generations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production transparent game sprite animation sheet, Jean elemental skill Gale Blade, a FORWARD WIND-PRESSURE CAST combined with a short centered sword thrust.
Create exactly 12 DISTINCT full-body poses in a strict 4-column 3-row layout, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom, on a 4:3 canvas. Genuine RGBA transparent background. Reference image is Jean basic.png for exact identity, clothing and sword construction, NOT its attack poses. Same adult woman with blonde high ponytail, blue ribbon, white fitted knight uniform, dark navy-blue split coat and gold trim, long dark boots, black gloves. Exquisite detailed Japanese anime painting matching reference; same mature proportions, same slender straight silver one-handed sword with ornate gold guard and blue center accent. Facing RIGHT in mild three-quarter side view.

CHOREOGRAPHY: She gathers wind inward by retracting her sword close to the RIGHT ribs and pressing her LEFT open palm inward; then steps half a pace to deliver one SHORT FORWARD CENTERLINE THRUST and a quick open empty left-palm push. This is not a rotational slash, not repeated jabs and not a permanent deep wide lunge. Wind-pressure generation is indicated by her concentrated closed body then clear release in frame05; avoid large painted magical FX because the game renders wind separately.

01: collected upright knight ready pose, feet in comfortable compact stagger, sword diagonally down toward right, empty left hand near waist, coat hangs quietly.
02: draw sword hand upward and backward toward right ribs, elbow closes to body, blade rotates toward horizontal forward, left palm moves inward in front of abdomen.
03: blade horizontal pointing right, sword hilt tucked at ribs and elbow behind torso, chest gently coils inward; empty left palm near centerline cupping gathered wind.
04: maximum compressed anticipation, sword held close at right ribs and aimed forward, left palm nearly closed toward chest, a tiny bend in knees; feet still compact. Sword tip is clearly retracted compared with frame05.
05: FIRST RELEASE AND CONTACT: short step to right, front knee only mildly bends, sword ALREADY driven out on straight chest-high centerline, left EMPTY palm also pushes outward beside the blade with fingers open. Confident clear forward wind-pressure release; torso advances only a little.
06: brief fullest arm extension, controlled weight over planted forward foot, blade horizontal right, empty palm reaches its brief push stop; coat/ponytail follow the single release motion.
07: both wrists brake, sword elbow begins softening, left palm recoil starts, no second swing and no renewed thrust.
08: sword arm retracts halfway from release to guard, left hand retracts close to chest, torso rising upright.
09: sword blade dips diagonally down right, weight shifts back toward center and legs draw closer.
10: recover sword wrist toward low guard and empty left arm relaxes, coat motion subsides.
11: comfortable upright compact stagger, sword down-forward and left hand nearly resting.
12: calm settled upright low guard like frame01, relaxed small shoulder motion, quiet hanging coat and ponytail.

Scale and framing are critical: one same fixed physical person, head size, body proportions, and sword length in every frame; never stretch or resize poses to fill cells. Target standing body height about240px on a1536x1152 sheet so the ENTIRE sword, every hair tip, fingers and both boots fit easily in each cell. Ground baseline stable per row. EVERY silhouette including sword is separated from every other pose by AT LEAST 32px completely transparent space horizontally AND vertically. Keep all pixels inside their own cells with at least16px empty margins. Do not let sword extend into next cell. Full character no cropping. No text, numbers, borders, grid lines, shadow blobs or floor. No motion streaks, arcs, auras, giant wind spheres or baked background. At most tiny pale teal blade-edge accent in frames03–06, do not obscure anatomy. Distinct inward preparation, outward release and settled recovery must be readable from the real poses.
generations.review: Forward-pressure choreography passed except frame04's sword was excessively foreshortened.

This entire move is ritual ASCENDING WIND GUIDANCE: the RIGHT hand holds the sword near the body and calmly pivots it into an upright conductor beside the chest/shoulder; the EMPTY LEFT hand scoops upward from waist to shoulder to summon and guide a front updraft. CLEAR EMPTY PALM-UP hand readable to the RIGHT of torso. No thrust, no broad uppercut slash, no lunge, no forward shove and no downward palm decree. Sword and empty hand jointly guide UPWARD. 12 sequential poses:
01: quiet standing low guard, sword diagonally down-right, empty left hand beside waist.
02: gather breath and lightly bend knees, right hand draws hilt near lower ribs, blade tips up gently; left empty palm turns upward at low abdomen.
03: right hilt rises toward chest so sword is steeply angled upward in front of body; left palm cups low near waist, fingers softly open.
04: compressed gathered wind pause, sword now nearly upright beside chest, elbow close; empty palm low and fully upward, focus aimed at point on RIGHT.
05 FIRST RELEASE: sword is upright beside RIGHT shoulder with hilt close chest and tip above head, and EMPTY LEFT hand ALREADY LIFTED from low waist to chest-height forward-right with palm upward and fingers lifting an invisible column. Torso starts to straighten. This is the first clear summon release.
06: complete upright extension, empty left palm rises to shoulder height with fingers upward, forearm elegantly tilted up; right sword remains upright and still beside body, hilt near chest, elbow bent. Feet stable.
07: sustain ascending guide, empty palm held upward and slightly forward above shoulder level, calm focused eyes, blade upright, no overarm strike.
08: sustain with slightly softer raised wrist and fingers, sword unchanged as vertical conductor; slight delayed lifting of coat tail and ponytail only.
09: slowly lower empty palm to shoulder height, maintaining palm-up while easing the summon, sword remains upright, shoulder begins to relax.
10: draw empty hand back toward chest and close fingers gently, sword hilt lowers and blade rotates forward-down in a compact controlled guard transition.
11: empty hand lowers beside body, sword diagonally down-right low guard, natural knight stance, cloth settling.
12: calm upright ready low guard, quiet ponytail and coat, same proportions as first pose.

Body scale and sword length fixed through all12 poses; sword blade never changes shape, disappears or becomes a rod.
